title: Antibiotics and Antimicrobial Resistance
text: Antibiotics are antimicrobial agents used to treat bacterial infections by killing bacteria or inhibiting their growth. Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928, marking the beginning of the antibiotic era. Antibiotics work through various mechanisms: inhibiting cell wall synthesis (penicillins), blocking protein synthesis (tetracyclines), or disrupting DNA replication (fluoroquinolones). Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) occurs when bacteria evolve mechanisms to withstand antibiotic attack, and is a growing global health threat. Overuse and misuse of antibiotics in human medicine and agriculture has accelerated the emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria, sometimes called superbugs.
